title: Registration, regime and deadlines
goal: The company knows whether and in which regime it is regulated, and tracks the deadlines from which it must comply with the measures.
summary: Act No. 264/2025 Coll., on Cybersecurity, has been effective since 1 November 2025 and transposes the NIS2 Directive into Czech law. It applies to providers of regulated services and divides them into two regimes: the lower-obligations regime (Decree No. 410/2025 Coll.) and the higher-obligations regime (Decree No. 409/2025 Coll.). The chapter explains how to find out whether the company is covered and in which regime, which deadlines run after registration, and how to work with this package. It is free: it also includes an overview of which requirements Atlas evidences and which the organization must evidence itself.

sections.title: 1. What the regulation requires
sections.html:
1. What the regulation requires

The Act imposes obligations on the provider of a regulated service. Regulated services and their assignment to a regime are set out in Decree No. 408/2025 Coll., on regulated services. Registration mainly concerns providers that operate in one of the sectors under the Act and are medium-sized or large enterprises; the detailed conditions are set out in Sec. 4 of the Act and in Decree No. 408/2025 Coll.

  • The higher-obligations regime applies to a provider that is of considerable economic, social or security importance for the Czech Republic (Sec. 8(1) of the Act); a service registered under Sec. 5 of the Act is always in the higher regime (Sec. 8(3)).
  • The lower-obligations regime applies to all other providers of regulated services.

The provider notifies the service itself. The National Cyber and Information Security Agency (NÚKIB) then decides on registration, and the deadlines for reporting data, implementing the measures and reporting incidents run from the delivery of the decision.

sections.title: 2. Rules
sections.html:
2. Rules

  • P-00-01Basic The company assesses whether it provides a regulated service and in which regime, and documents the conclusion and the supporting documents.
  • P-00-02Basic It notifies NÚKIB of the regulated service within 60 days at the latest from the day on which it began to meet the conditions for registration.
  • P-00-03Basic Within 30 days of the delivery of the registration decision, it reports the contact and supplementary data; it reports changes to them within 14 days.
  • P-00-04Basic It notifies NÚKIB of changes to the regulated service that may lead to a change of regime within 60 days at the latest.
  • P-00-05Basic It has the delivery date of the registration decision on record and plans around it: no later than one year after delivery, it must comply with the security measures and report cybersecurity incidents.

sections.title: 4. How to evidence it
sections.html:
4. How to evidence it

  • Record of the assessment: which services the company provides, how they were classified under Decree No. 408/2025 Coll., and why.
  • Confirmation of the service notification and the registration decision with its delivery date.
  • Record of the contact and supplementary data reported and of their changes.
  • Deadline calendar: reporting of data (30 days), implementation of the measures and incident reporting (1 year from the delivery of the decision).

sections.title: 5. What Atlas evidences
sections.html:
5. What Atlas evidences

Each rule in the package carries one of three marks. They show what Atlas evidences and what the organization must evidence itself.

  • Atlas verifies – Atlas can measure the requirement in Microsoft 365: an open finding of the corresponding Atlas rule means that the requirement is not met. Without a finding, this is evidence for Microsoft 365, not for systems outside it.
  • Atlas supports – Atlas provides supporting material (an inventory, a list of roles, an audit record, an access snapshot, a record of an intervention), but the organization decides whether the requirement is met.
  • The organization evidences – this is a document, decision, contract, training or physical measure. Atlas has no data for it and claims nothing.

Rules have three levels. Basic are the requirements of Act No. 264/2025 Coll. and Decree No. 410/2025 Coll. that apply in both regimes. Standard are the requirements that Decree No. 409/2025 Coll. additionally imposes for the higher regime. Advanced is a recommendation beyond the regulation. The assessment target follows the regime set for the package: the lower regime assesses Basic, the higher regime Basic and Standard.

The rules of this chapter are evidenced only by the organization. Atlas measures nothing in it.
